item.description:
Thursday, September 3 • 5:00 pm – 10:00 pm | From $61.33 Event Details and Tickets Come join us for a night of live music on the outdoor stage as part of the French Broad River Brewery Summer Concert Series! The Movement: The Movement has been winning the hearts and minds of alt-reggae fans since their inception in 2003.Drawing inspiration from Sublime, 311, Slightly Stoopid, and John Brown’s Body, they’ve made a name for themselves as reggae shapeshifters with a foundation of insightful lyrics and heavy drum and bass.
“Kona Dub-Rock.” That’s how Pepper describes their blend of reggae, alternative rock, dub, island rhythms, and punk rock energy. It’s a sound that’s taken the trio from the Big Island of Hawaii — where vocalist/guitarist Kaleo Wassman, vocalist/bassist Bret Bollinger, and drummer Yesod Williams held their first band practice as teenagers in the late 1990s — to the upper reaches of Billboard’s Reggae Albums chart, where 2019’s Local Motion peaked at Number 1.

item.title: Feed and Seed Bluegrass — Fri Aug 28, 7:00 PM
item.description:
Hendo Fun Friends FRIDAY, AUGUST 28 ; Lynn Goldsmith & The Jeter Mountain Band \* 7:00 – 9:00 Feed & Seed is a former Feed store that has been converted to a church. It is famous for great bluegrass music performances at no charge to the public. The bands play for tips. The concession stand is inexpensive and the music is priceless. The local clog dancers alone are enough reason to go. Arrive early to secure a parking space and a seat. Parking is available behind the building on Fanning Bridge Rd. Enter thru the side. A Blue Ridge Music Trails of NC site. https://feedandseednc.com/
Source: Hendo Fun Friends

item.title: Mountains Region Entomology Season Summit — Sat Aug 29, 10:00 AM
item.description:
Mountains Region Entomology Season Summit August 29th, 2026 @ 10:00 am Location: The North Carolina Arboretum Registration is required for this event. Register Here! Grab your antennas and buzz on down to the NC Arboretum to celebrate the end of Entomology Field Season with local entomologist, Robbie Zinna of Mars Hill University! We’ll meet in the Playing Woods outdoor classroom then venture out on a search to see what different types of flying and terrestrial insects we can find around the NC Arboretum! We’ll have games, activities, and you guessed it – bugs!
This event is for kids aged 5 – 13 years old and accompanying adults. CONTACT: ecoexplore@ncarboretum.org Parking fees for the arboretum will be waived for ecoEXPLORE program registrants. Attending this event counts towards Entomology Challenge #4
Source: NC Arboretum

item.title: Group Channel Practice Meeting (online) — Sun Aug 30, 1:00 PM
item.description:
Awakening Asheville This meeting is for experienced and beginner channels to come together to learn and practice channeling. All types of channeling are welcome, including written, verbal, and light language.
The intention is to bring us together in a safe, energetic space to learn, share, and lift each other's vibration and access to wisdom, for the highest good of all.
We will start with questions and discussion on channeling, if needed, and then I'll guide us into an open, pure-love energy field to play with channeling together. If you're new to channeling and not yet comfortable doing it in front of others, feel free to come and simply listen.
Once channeling has started you indicate you would like do verbal or light language by un-muting yourself and beginning. When you finish just mute yourself to let others know the space is open.
Source: Awakening Asheville

item.title: Fiber Friends — Sat Sep 5, 10:00 AM — 23 Ed Parlor
item.description:
UU Asheville Fiber Friends is a group of crafters who do handwork on personal projects and for the community. Mainly knitters and crocheters, we create warm items for donation to local charities (serving children, youth, and adults) and make a variety of cotton cloths given to Meals on Wheels for their “Santa for seniors” packages each December. A limited supply of yarn and tools (needles and hooks) are also available.
Join us the first Saturday of each month in the parlor of 23 Edwin, from 10 AM until about 12 noon. For more information or to be added to the monthly email reminder list, contact Mara Sprain.
Source: Unitarian Universalist Congregation of Asheville

Experience the magic of Sound Baths in the Gardens. While relaxing amongst the flora, be soothed by the sounds of unique instruments used to reset your nervous system. This 60-minute pause from your day-to-day will be nestled in the gardens of The NC Arboretum: a nature home away from home. If it’s raining, don’t worry. There is a beautiful indoor space with large windows overlooking the forest so you can still soak in the magic without being actually soaked. Your ticket grants you access into The NC Arboretum (feel free to explore their exhibits afterwards!). You can bring your own mat or borrow one of ours for $5. Senseful Soul’s Asheville Healing Community🧘🏻‍♀️🏳️‍🌈🪐🔮 oin Senseful Wellness for some astrology explanation and New Moon inspired yoga flow. Meet Senseful Wellness at the Botanical gardens by UNCA for class themed around the new moon.
Together we will : \- Disccuss what the New Moon is asking from us \- Flow through a New Moon inspired sequence \- Journal & Reflect on the New Moon
What to bring: Journal & Pen Water
We will have Yoga Mats and additional props but you are welcome to bring your own.
This is a Donation Based Event Recommended Donation $10 - $25
